title: Ten Fictional Men Who Still Teach Us About Character
author: Chris Martin
source: The Ways of a Gentleman (Martin Substack), January 24, 2026
summary: Martin argues that literature and film preserve models of masculine character that contemporary culture often lacks or actively undermines. He profiles ten fictional characters—from classic literature and film—who exemplify various dimensions of ideal manhood: courage, integrity, loyalty, sacrifice, and humility. These characters range from historical figures reimagined in literature to entirely fictional creations, but all share the capacity to face difficulty with grace, to keep their word, to serve something larger than themselves, and to earn the respect of those around them through action rather than words. Martin contends that engaging with these fictional models is not escapism but a form of cultural education—young men learn what to aspire to by encountering these characters in stories. The modern abandonment of literature in favor of entertainment has impoverished the cultural transmission of masculine ideals.
points: Literature and film preserve models of masculine character that contemporary culture often lacks or actively undermines—engagement with these stories is cultural education.
Great fictional characters exemplify dimensions of ideal manhood: courage, integrity, loyalty, sacrifice, and humility—character traits that are increasingly rare in contemporary examples.
Young men learn what to aspire to by encountering these characters in stories, but modern entertainment culture has replaced literature with content that lacks such depth.
The fictional characters who endure across generations are those who face difficulty with grace, keep their word, serve something larger than themselves, and earn respect through action.
The abandonment of literature in favor of entertainment has impoverished the cultural transmission of masculine ideals and left young men without adequate models to emulate.
